blocks.text: What went well
Ratings were strong overall, with several attendees calling the presentations and format excellent.
Both panel topics (digital equipment investment and tech ROI) scored well for value.
Strong interest in follow-up programs like the AI Conductor and Industry Exchange.
Attendees appreciated the networking opportunities at the event.
Several attendees are already interested in developing or expanding training programs.
Areas to improve
Give panels more time and trim lengthy panelist introductions.
Post wifi access info, and consider moving the survey to a digital format.
Focus more panel content specifically on small and midsized manufacturers.
Have tour host companies highlight new technologies rather than a general facility walkthrough.
Prep panelists in advance with clearer expectations to reduce predictable, generic answers.
What went well
Attendees valued the mix of company sizes and appreciated the small-business representation.
Several called out the panel content itself as a strong part of the meeting.
Attendees expressed strong interest in learning more about AI Conductor and real-world use cases.
The variety of industries represented was noted as a highlight for networking.
Multiple attendees want to keep going deeper on AI topics, showing high engagement with the content.
Areas to improve
Keep speakers and panelists on their allotted time slots.
Improve audio and increase slide text size so everyone can hear and read clearly.
Add a way to exchange business cards or attendee info at the start of the meeting.
Stay on schedule so the full agenda doesn't get cut short.
Set aside dedicated time after lunch for panel Q&A and networking.
What went well
Attendees gave strong marks across meeting value and both content sessions.
The site tour and Q&A drew enthusiastic praise from multiple attendees.
Several called out the strong presentation pacing and content quality.
Attendees appreciated a full room and high engagement at the event.
Multiple organizations expressed interest in learning more about Conexus programs.
Areas to improve
Send more pre-meeting details ahead of site tours.
Have keynote speakers elaborate more on their own programs.
Add a session featuring current or former students sharing their experience.
Cover soft-skills development for high school-aged workforce topics.
Continue building employer understanding of their role in workforce development.
What went well
Ratings were consistently positive across logistics, meeting value, and both content sessions.
Attendees showed strong interest in follow-up programs like the AML ITA and AI Use Case Catalog.
Multiple organizations offered leads for council membership, showing good engagement.
One university offered to host a future meeting, signaling a strong relationship.
A speaker offered to present on economic outlook for a future session.
Areas to improve
Reduce the morning tour to one stop instead of two to ease the schedule.
Provide presentation materials to attendees afterward.
Add a key or legend to data slides for clarity.
Cover tariff, foreign trade, and economic development topics in future sessions.
Ratings dipped slightly on the workforce and employer panel sessions compared to overall meeting value.
What went well
Attendees called it the best CIAIC meeting yet, and several praised the opening remarks and sense of connection.
The event drew strong satisfaction scores across logistics, meeting value, and both presentations.
The economic outlook and AI panel sessions were consistently rated highly by attendees.
Several attendees said the meeting sparked real interest in networking and partner connections.
Multiple organizations expressed enthusiasm about future participation, including one offering to host.
Areas to improve
Add a way for attendees to share company info or connect with peers they want to meet.
Provide microphones for audience Q&A.
One attendee felt the AI panel leaned too heavily into a vendor sales pitch.
Add a resource highlighting relevant trade shows for Indiana manufacturers.
Include more real-world case studies of successful tech implementations.
What went well
Attendees loved the economic and tariff discussion, calling it informative and well done.
The AI applications breakout session was praised for strong use cases and Q&A.
Printed materials, pens, and a well-chosen meeting venue drew specific praise.
One attendee called it their favorite meeting yet, highlighting both main presentations.
Interest in real-world case studies and industry speakers came through as a strong draw.
Areas to improve
Send the agenda and presentations a week in advance so attendees can prepare and take notes.
Include attendee names and companies in the handouts for easier networking.
Give tours more time so all areas can be adequately covered.
Make the AI presentation more dynamic, since some speakers struggled to hold attention.
Add clearer takeaways or a roadmap after discussion-heavy sessions, not just open conversation.
What went well
The infrastructure expert panel and freight bottleneck discussion drew the most praise.
The Beck site tour impressed attendees, especially the visible Industry 4.0 technology.
Rep. Shreve's legislative perspective was singled out as the most insightful content.
Roundtable and group discussion time created real peer-to-peer business connections.
Advance materials scored highest of any question — logistics and prep were clear.
Areas to improve
Several attendees found the topics only partly relevant to their own role or sector.
Not all questions submitted through the QR code got answered.
Attendees want short pre-reads or articles to prepare for discussion topics.
The Federal Overview and Q&A scored lowest of the two sessions.
One member asked for a clearer channel to get industry freight plans in front of INDOT
What went well
The workshop format landed well, with multiple attendees calling for at least two per year.
Workforce development and State of the Workforce content were repeatedly called out as most impactful.
Networking was highlighted as a standout, alongside strong overall organization and communication.
The employer site tour and employment data were noted as insightful.
Several attendees simply praised the event as consistently well-run and enjoyable.
Areas to improve
Send workshop materials in advance so attendees can prepare thoughts beforehand.
Start afternoon tours earlier to close the gap between the meeting ending and the tour starting.
Build in more biobreaks during the agenda.
Have member companies present their own case studies as part of the program.
Address how attendees can better tap into and use the council network itself.
What went well
The AI presentation and MRG Impact Report were repeatedly cited as the most valuable content.
Attendees called the facility tours and site visits a highlight, sparking new ideas to bring home.
Several called this one of the best meetings they've attended, praising the networking.
The company review sessions (e.g., Arcamed) resonated strongly with attendees.
Guest speakers were seen as a standout, with one described as a "game changer."
Areas to improve
Add an attendee list and clearer ways to connect, such as company info cards or a networking area.
Give more real-world, practical examples alongside the presentations.
Provide handouts like QR codes or electronic copies of reports for attendees to keep.
Moderate Q&A time better and offer an after-session chat for detailed follow-up questions.
Make name badges easier to read (larger company names).
What went well
Dr. Jenner's presentation was a standout, with multiple attendees praising her clarity and passion.
The High School Redesign and youth apprenticeship content resonated strongly with attendees.
Attendees valued the meetings' focus on real problems, real solutions, and collaboration.
The diploma and apprenticeship explanations were called out as especially helpful.
The broader tie between education and community/business development landed well.
Areas to improve
Add more Q&A time for attendees to dig into topics.
Share concrete examples of companies successfully implementing work-based learning.
Help new or less-connected attendees know who to network with at lunch.
Provide more detail on success stories behind the high school redesign and apprenticeships.
Address extracurricular/STEM pathway credit (e.g., robotics, alternative-fuel programs) toward employment recognition.
What went well
Lippert University's workforce training content was one of the most praised topics across attendees.
Splitting the meeting into regional sites made attendance easier, especially for southern-region members.
The AV Freight Readiness and electrification content felt timely and relevant to attendees' businesses.
Speaker energy and delivery drew specific praise, keeping the room engaged.
Attendees valued hearing directly from researchers and peer companies about real progress versus hype.
Areas to improve
Improve projection and slide visibility, since some presentations were hard to see.
Clarify meeting location instructions in advance to avoid confusion.
Provide more takeaway materials beyond the slides for detailed topics.
Some content felt too far out to act on; attendees prefer more near-term, actionable topics.
Fix pre-meeting communication delivery so materials reliably reach all attendees.
What went well
Several attendees called it the best meeting to date, praising strong organization and content.
Speakers like Elisabeth Reynolds and Katie Culp were repeatedly singled out for expertise and insight.
Attendees valued the facility tour and seeing real-world automation in action.
Content on grants, tax incentives, and energy solutions gave attendees actionable next steps.
Networking and connecting with new contacts continued to stand out as a highlight.
Areas to improve
Improve audio quality, especially for tours held on noisy warehouse floors.
Break sessions into smaller chunks to help hold attention throughout the day.
Share more background on host companies in advance of facility tours.
Add a facilitated roundtable discussion format to complement presentations.
Provide more specifics on how smaller and mid-sized manufacturers can access opportunities.
What went well
Subaru's real-world Industry 4.0 and IIOT implementation story was repeatedly cited as the most impactful content.
Chico Marks' practical, video-based presentation was called one of the best the group has seen.
The TEConomy research and state comparison data landed well and sparked good questions.
New members praised the communication and coordination leading up to the meeting.
Attendees valued networking and meeting new peers as much as the content itself.
Areas to improve
Add more Q&A time and have speakers repeat or hold the mic for questions so the room can hear.
Share an attendee list to make networking easier.
Send pre-read data (like the TEConomy report) further ahead so attendees can prepare questions.
Clarify how Industry 4.0 content applies to smaller companies and suppliers, not just large ones.
Add small-group discussion time to break up the large-format presentations.
